title: Pizza Prosciutto e Funghi
subtitle: Ham and mushroom pizza
excerpt: Pizza prosciutto e funghi is one of the most ordered pizzas in Italian restaurants outside Italy. Tomato, mozzarella, sauteed mushrooms, and prosciutto crudo or cooked ham on a thin crust. The mushrooms need a quick fry before they go on so they do not make the base soggy.
sourceNotes: Pizza prosciutto e funghi is one of the most common pizzeria combinations across Italy and the Italian diaspora. It predates formal documentation and is considered a standard of the Italian pizzeria menu.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. Fry the mushrooms and set aside before starting to shape the dough.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat with a heavy tray or pizza stone inside for 45 minutes.

content.text: This is a ham and mushroom pizza: tomato sauce, mozzarella, finely sliced chestnut mushrooms, and prosciutto. The key step is frying the mushrooms before they go on. Raw mushrooms release water as they cook on the pizza and make the base soft and pale. A quick fry drives off that moisture and turns them golden and slightly meaty.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per pizza, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.

items.prepNote: or cooked ham, torn into strips

content.text: Heat the oven to its maximum setting with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for at least 45 minutes.
Fry the mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of olive oil over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden. Season with salt and set aside.
Season the passata with salt. Stretch one dough ball to a rough 30 cm disc.
Spread the passata over the base, scatter the mozzarella, then spread the mushrooms over the top. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the rim is charred and the mozzarella is bubbling. Remove from the oven and lay the prosciutto strips over the hot pizza. Eat immediately.

attrs.title: Ham: on before or after?
attrs.body: If you use prosciutto crudo, add it after baking. The heat from the pizza wilts it gently without turning it chewy. If you use cooked ham, add it on top of the mushrooms before the pizza goes in the oven.

content.text: Ham and mushroom pizza is one of the most ordered combinations in Italian restaurants outside Italy. Inside Italy it is a reliable pizzeria standard, though Italians would argue over whether the ham should go on before or after baking. Adding prosciutto crudo after the oven is the more careful treatment; cooked ham goes in with the mushrooms.
